title: Token surge stabilizer: degenerate-path handling and fairness heuristics
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Production traffic frequently includes short-lived surges (e.g., client retries, onboarding spikes, scheduled batch jobs) that push local limiter instances into degenerate behavior: token buckets drain, queued requests pile up behind overloaded nodes, and failover to other regions amplifies bursts due to naïve retry/fanout.

Objective: Implement a Token Surge Stabilizer subsystem to prevent degenerate limiter paths during bursts and limiter outages. The stabilizer should smooth short spikes, preserve fairness across tenants and routes, and provide safe degraded modes when central quota metadata is unreachable.

Key Goals:
- Reduce transient p95/p99 tail latency caused by limiter contention during spikes.
- Maintain per-customer fairness: avoid noisy neighbors consuming disproportionate shared burst capacity.
- Provide principled degraded behavior during limiter outages with clear metrics and observability.

Scope: Changes span the limiter service, local admission control, and multi-region failover routing heuristics. No public API changes expected.
acceptance_criteria: New stabilizer reduces region-local p99 latency from limiter queuing by >= 30% on synthetic spike workloads
Fairness regression tests show top-1 tenant share of burst capacity <= 40% on mixed-tenancy synthetic workloads
Limiter outage degraded mode maintains 90th percentile success rate for high-priority routes while returning clear 429/503 semantics for overloaded lower-priority routes
Automated canary run (10% traffic) for 48 hours with no SLO regression on core text-generation endpoints
implementation_steps: Design stabilizer: combine short-term token bump smoothing, fair-share dampening, and an emergency token reservoir with backpressure gates
Add local in-memory short-window reservoir per node to absorb microbursts (100-500ms horizon) with LRU per-customer accounting
Implement fairness scheduler that uses exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of recent consumption per customer to weight admission during shortages
Define degraded modes: (A) isolated-accept for priority customers, (B) regional-shed where low-priority routes return 429, (C) global-fallback routing to other regions with jittered retry throttles
Integrate health-checks: limiter sync heartbeat and draining protocol for nodes entering degraded mode
Build observability: per-node reservoir fill, per-customer EWMA, shed-rate, and degraded-mode events surfaced to Console dashboards and alerting
rollout_plan: Unit tests + deterministic fairness harness in CI
Dogfood on internal traffic with feature flag (stabilizer=on) for non-critical routes
Canary to 10% of production traffic in a single region for 48h (runtime-1.22-canary). Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and fairness metrics
Progressively enable across regions with staggered start times and increased traffic windows (10% -> 30% -> 70% -> 100%)
If degradation detected, automatic roll-back via feature-flag and fail-open behavior to previous admission logic
metrics: Per-tenant burst-share (windowed): fraction of absorbed burst tokens
Cross-region failover amplification ratio (requests forwarded vs. originating)
risks: Reservoir introduces state that must be resilient to node restarts; mismanaged state could unfairly advantage some tenants
EWMA tuning may be sensitive to workload shapes (long-tail customers vs. short aggressive bursts)
Aggressive degraded modes could create customer-visible errors for low-priority routes if misclassified
Cross-region retries without jitter could amplify bursts elsewhere (retry storm)
testing_plan: Deterministic unit tests for scheduler and reservoir semantics
Load test scenarios: single-tenant spike, multi-tenant mixed bursts, cross-region outage with retry storms
Chaos tests: limiter process crash/restart, simulated cluster partition and late state reconciliation
E2E canary with synthetic SLO checks and synthetic attacker scenarios (one tenant saturating 80% of requests)
